slides.title: Blow fiber in, don't pull it
No winch. No rope. Just compressed air.
slides.body: A crew can move cable several hundred metres in about twenty minutes.

slides.title: What a microduct is
slides.body: A small HDPE tube, about 5 to 16 mm across. Sizes read outside over inside: 7/5.5, 10/8, 12/10, 14/10 mm.

slides.title: How blowing works
slides.body: Drive wheels push the cable while air flows past it. Drag along the whole length carries it forward.

slides.title: Why it goes so far
slides.body: A rope pull puts all the force at the eye and multiplies it at bends. Blowing spreads it, so 1 km+ is possible.

slides.title: Civils once, cable many times
slides.body: Lay the duct bundle once. Blow cables only when customers sign up. Upgrade by blowing one out and another in.

slides.title: The duct must be perfect
slides.body: Clean, dry, continuous and capped from day one. Pressure test and send a sponge through before every blow.

Once you have seen fiber blown into a duct, rope pulling looks slow.

Microducts are small HDPE tubes, and compressed air carries a microcable through them for hundreds of metres. The bigger win is money: dig once, add cable as customers sign up. Swipe for how it works and what breaks it.
